title: The Garage & Mechanic
strapline: Bring your car in for a check-up — up on the ramp, spanners out, tyres pumped, and back on the road as good as new.
intent: The mechanic who fixes cars, bikes and vehicles is a fascinating community helper, and playing out a garage lets children explore how things work and the people who mend them.
Using spanners, pumps and tools on real or pretend vehicles builds strong fine-motor control, hand strength and eye-hand coordination.
Diagnosing what's wrong, taking things apart and putting them back together is genuine problem-solving, sequencing and early engineering.
The garage is full of mathematics — measuring, counting bolts and tyres, checking tyre pressure numbers, matching tools to jobs.
Booking cars in, writing repair notes and giving bills to customers grows conversation and gives writing and number a real job.
Real vocabulary and knowledge grow — mechanic, engine, spanner, tyre, pump, repair, tool, fix.
implementation: Set up a garage — real spanners and tools (child-safe), a foot pump, ride-on cars or bikes to mend, a ramp, overalls and a repair book.
Take a customer's role bringing a poorly vehicle in: 'My bike's making a funny noise and the tyre's flat — can you find out what's wrong and fix it?'
Model the diagnosing talk: 'Let's check it over. What do you think the problem is? Which tool will you need for that?'
Bring in maths through the play — count and sort the bolts and tools, measure and check the tyres, tally the repairs, write out the bill.
Weave in real knowledge of how things work — what makes a wheel turn, why a tyre needs air — and let children take apart and reassemble safe objects.
Add a booking-in book, repair notes and invoices for real writing, and let the workshop stay busy with a queue of vehicles to mend.
key_questions: What do you think the problem is? Which tool will you need for that?
Can you find out what's wrong and fix it?
How many bolts have you taken out?
Is this tyre pumped up enough — how could we check?
How much shall we write on the bill?
